column3: But a man named Ananias, together with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,
and with his wife’s knowledge he kept back part of the price and brought a certain part and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart for you to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the price of the land?
While it remained, did it not remain yours? And after it was sold, was it not in your authority? Why did you put this deed in your heart? You did not lie to people but to God.”
When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last, and great fear came upon all who heard about it.
And the young men got up, wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him.
Now an interval of about three hours passed, and his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter responded to her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for this much.” She said, “Yes, for this much.”
Peter said to her, “Why was it agreed by you to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”
Immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. When the young men came in, they found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
And great fear came upon the whole assembly and upon all who heard these things.
Now through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were happening among the people, and they were all together with one accord in Solomon’s Portico.
None of the rest dared to join them, but the people were speaking highly of them.
Yet believers were being added to the Lord in even greater numbers, multitudes of both men and women,
so that they even carried the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and mats, so that when Peter came by, at least his shadow might fall on some of them.
The multitude from the cities around Jerusalem was also gathering, bringing sick people and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all being healed.
But the high priest rose up, and all those with him, which was the sect of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy.
They laid hands on the apostles and put them in the public prison.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors, brought them out, and said,
“Go, stand in the temple and speak to the people all the words of this life.”

When they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began teaching. But when the high priest and those with him arrived, they called together the council and all the senate of the sons of Israel and sent to the prison to have them brought.
But the officers who came did not find them in the prison, so they returned and reported,
“We found the prison shut with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened it, we found no one inside.”
Now when both the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were greatly perplexed about them as to what this might become.
But someone came and reported to them, “Look, the men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.”
Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, not with force, for they feared the people, lest they be stoned.
After bringing them, they stood them before the council. And the high priest questioned them,
saying, “We strictly commanded you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.”
But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than people.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.
God exalted this one to his right hand as Leader and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God gave to those obeying him.”
When they heard this, they were cut to the heart and were intending to kill them.
But a Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law honored by all the people, stood up and ordered the men to be put outside for a short time.
Then he said to them, “Men of Israel, pay attention to yourselves concerning these men, what you are about to do.

For before these days Theudas rose up, saying that he himself was somebody, and a number of about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all who were persuaded by him were scattered and came to nothing.
After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew people away after him. That man also perished, and all who were persuaded by him were dispersed.
And now I tell you, stay away from these men and leave them alone, because if this plan or this work is from people, it will be overthrown;
but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them. You may even be found fighting against God.” And they were persuaded by him.
And after calling the apostles in, they beat them and commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
So they went out from the presence of the council rejoicing that they had been considered worthy to be dishonored for the Name.
And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and announcing the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
